purpose: Teach policy as an operating design that defines purpose, allowed and prohibited uses, data rules, human authority, review, records, incidents, exceptions, and revision.
staffSummary: Build M30 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Draft a policy rule that a real employee can apply to a real utility task and that a reviewer can test. The learner must leave with a usable AI and data policy operating kit, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: Employees already use several assistants, but the organization's policy says only use AI responsibly and gives no practical direction.
learnerDecision: Draft a policy rule that a real employee can apply to a real utility task and that a reviewer can test.
analogy: A standard operating procedure works because it names the steps, limits, checks, and stop conditions. A useful policy must also guide action.
learnerOutcomes: Explain Policy by Design: Writing AI and Data Policies in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish principle, policy, standard, procedure, control, exception, incident, and review without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Policy language requires legal, labor, privacy, security, records, procurement, accessibility, and operational review. A course template is not legal approval.
Create a usable AI and data policy operating kit with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give Policy by Design: Writing AI and Data Policies one clear learning job inside Governance, Security and Provenance.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the AI and data policy operating kit.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Draft a policy rule that a real employee can apply to a real utility task and that a reviewer can test.
Name the AI and data policy operating kit as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
requiredWorkProduct: AI and data policy operating kit
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete AI and data policy operating kit, and names the next accountable action.
scopeBoundary: Policy language requires legal, labor, privacy, security, records, procurement, accessibility, and operational review. A course template is not legal approval.
